newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Moslem militants clash with police in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Moslem militants clash with police in Pakistan.

text.p: Activists from a militant Sunni Moslem faction pelted police with stones on Friday in Karachi, southern Pakistan, during a protest at the appointment of a provincial minister from a minority sect.

About 250 activists of the Sunni Tehrik (Movement) launched their action in a commercial district to protest at a member of the Ahmadi religious sect being included in the Sindh provincial government.
Sunni Tehrik and other militant Moslem factions regard the Ahmadi as heretical.
The protesters prayed in the road and then tried to march on the Sindh Chief Minister's House to stage a sit-in, but were forced back by police.
Angry young activists threw stones at the police and smashed about a dozen cars parked nearby. No one was injured.
Sunni Tehrik and other militant Moslem factions were angered by the inclusion of Kanwar Idris as interior and town planning minister in the caretaker provincial cabinet.

Idris belongs to the Ahmadi community, officially declared to be outside the pale of Islam by parliament in 1974. In 1984 a decree banned Ahmadis from using Islamic forms of worship or describing their places of worship as mosques.
